description: Finish the TTS module implementation to provide voice announcements during workouts. This includes interval changes, target power callouts, motivational cues, and customizable voice settings.

phases.name: Core TTS Implementation
phases.description: Implement the actual TTS functionality using the tts crate, replacing the stub implementations.

subtasks.title: Implement TTS crate integration
subtasks.description: Replace the stub DefaultTtsProvider with actual tts crate calls. Initialize the TTS engine properly, implement speak() and speak_async() methods using tts::Tts, and handle platform-specific initialization for Windows (SAPI), macOS (NSSpeechSynthesizer), and Linux (speech-dispatcher).
subtasks.notes: The tts crate v0.26 is already in Cargo.toml. Must handle platform-specific errors gracefully. COMPLETED: Implemented actual tts::Tts integration with lazy initialization, platform-specific error messages, and proper speak()/speak_async() implementations.

subtasks.title: Implement voice enumeration and selection
subtasks.description: Replace the hardcoded voice list with actual system voice enumeration from the tts crate. Implement get_voices() to return real voices with proper language codes, and implement set_voice() to actually change the TTS voice.
subtasks.notes: COMPLETED: Implemented real voice enumeration using tts.voices() and voice selection using tts.set_voice(). get_voices() maps tts::Voice to VoiceInfo with id, name, language, and is_default. set_voice() finds the matching voice by ID and actually sets it in the TTS engine. Tests updated to work with dynamic voice lists and handle CI environments.

subtasks.title: Implement rate and volume controls
subtasks.description: Wire up set_rate() and set_volume() to actually affect TTS output. The tts crate supports rate and volume settings. Ensure proper clamping and normalization between our 0-1 range and the tts crate's expected ranges.
subtasks.notes: COMPLETED: Rate and volume controls were already implemented in subtask 1.1. set_rate() clamps to 0.5-2.0 (where 1.0 is normal speed), set_volume() clamps to 0.0-1.0. Both are applied via apply_rate() and apply_volume() helper methods, called during initialization and before each speak/speak_async operation. The tts crate 0.26 uses f32 values directly for both.

subtasks.title: Add TTS state management and thread safety
subtasks.description: The tts crate's Tts struct is not Send+Sync on all platforms. Create a proper wrapper that handles TTS calls on a dedicated thread if needed. Implement proper is_speaking() tracking.
subtasks.notes: COMPLETED: Implemented ThreadSafeTtsProvider that handles TTS operations on a dedicated worker thread. Added TtsCommand enum for thread communication, proper is_speaking() tracking using Arc<AtomicBool>, clean shutdown via Drop trait, and comprehensive tests. The worker thread owns the tts::Tts instance and processes commands via channel, making it safe to use from multiple threads on all platforms including macOS.

phases.name: Audio Engine Integration
phases.description: Connect the TTS provider to the audio engine and implement the speech queue.

subtasks.title: Wire TTS provider into AudioEngine
subtasks.description: Update DefaultAudioEngine to hold and use the TTS provider. The speak() method should delegate to the TTS provider with proper configuration (rate, volume from AudioConfig).
subtasks.notes: COMPLETED: Implemented TTS integration in DefaultAudioEngine: added ThreadSafeTtsProvider field, updated new() to create and configure TTS provider with voice_volume and speech_rate from AudioConfig, initialize() now initializes TTS and sets preferred voice, speak() delegates to TTS provider with proper configuration, stop() now stops TTS playback. Added tts_provider() accessor and update_config() helper methods.

subtasks.title: Implement speech queuing with priority
subtasks.description: Ensure the AudioEngine's queue properly handles Speech items. High-priority speech (like interval changes) should interrupt lower-priority items. Implement stop() to actually stop current speech.
subtasks.notes: COMPLETED: Implemented priority-based interruption in AudioEngine. Added current_priority tracking, interrupt_requested flag, should_interrupt() logic for High/Critical priorities. High-priority items now interrupt lower-priority playback and clear the queue. stop() now properly stops TTS, clears queue, and resets state. Added speak_with_interrupt_check() for monitored speech. Comprehensive tests added for interrupt logic, queue clearing, and state management.

subtasks.title: Add TTS configuration persistence
subtasks.description: Save and load TTS settings (preferred voice, rate, volume) from the config store. Integrate with the existing AudioConfig serialization.
subtasks.notes: COMPLETED: Added AudioConfig to AppConfig for persistent storage. Changes: 1) Added AudioConfig field to AppConfig with #[serde(default)] for backwards compatibility, 2) Updated app.rs to use config.audio.clone() instead of AudioConfig::default(), 3) Added example_audio_config() for documentation, 4) Added load_audio_config() helper function, 5) Added comprehensive tests for serialization/deserialization including full config, missing audio section, and partial config scenarios.

phases.name: Workout Event Integration
phases.description: Connect workout events to voice announcements.

subtasks.title: Create workout audio bridge
subtasks.description: Create a WorkoutAudioBridge component that subscribes to WorkoutEngine events and triggers appropriate alerts via the AlertManager. This bridges the gap between workout events and the audio system.
subtasks.notes: COMPLETED: Created WorkoutAudioBridge component with WorkoutAudioBridgeConfig for controlling announcements (interval_changes, countdowns, workout_lifecycle, trainer_status, recovery_intervals). Implemented process_events()/process_event() async methods that map all WorkoutEvent variants to AlertType/AlertContext. Comprehensive test suite with MockAlertManager.

subtasks.title: Implement interval change announcements
subtasks.description: When an interval changes, announce the interval name, target power, and duration. Use the CueBuilder to generate natural-sounding messages like 'Sweet Spot interval, 260 watts, 5 minutes'.
subtasks.notes: COMPLETED: Updated IntervalChange template to include power in natural-sounding format. Template now produces messages like 'Sweet Spot interval, 260 watts, 5 minutes'. Added graceful handling for missing power values (removes placeholder and cleans up surrounding commas). Added comprehensive tests for various durations and edge cases.

subtasks.title: Implement countdown announcements
subtasks.description: Announce countdown before interval changes (10, 5, 3, 2, 1 seconds). The WorkoutEngine already emits IntervalCountdown events at these thresholds.
subtasks.notes: COUNTDOWN_THRESHOLDS is already defined in workout engine.

subtasks.title: Add motivational cues
subtasks.description: Add optional motivational messages during high-intensity intervals ('You're doing great!', 'Keep pushing!') and recovery intervals ('Nice work, catch your breath'). Make these configurable.
subtasks.notes: Should be optional and not too frequent to avoid annoyance.

phases.name: Voice Settings UI
phases.description: Add voice selection and configuration to the settings screen.

subtasks.title: Add voice selection dropdown to settings
subtasks.description: Add a dropdown/combo box to the Voice Alerts section in settings that lists available system voices. Allow users to select their preferred voice.
subtasks.notes: The settings screen already has the Voice Alerts section with volume and rate sliders.

subtasks.title: Add voice preview button
subtasks.description: Add a 'Test' or 'Preview' button next to the voice selection that speaks a sample phrase ('This is how your voice alerts will sound') so users can preview voices before selecting.
subtasks.notes: Should use the currently selected voice settings.

subtasks.title: Add per-alert-type voice configuration
subtasks.description: In the expanded audio alerts section, allow users to customize which alert types use voice vs. sound effects. Some users may want only interval changes spoken but not countdowns.
subtasks.notes: AlertConfig already has use_voice and play_sound fields.

phases.name: Testing and Platform Verification
phases.description: Ensure TTS works correctly on all supported platforms.

subtasks.title: Add TTS integration tests
subtasks.description: Create integration tests that verify TTS initialization, voice enumeration, and speech on each platform. Tests should handle cases where TTS is not available gracefully.
subtasks.notes: TTS availability varies by platform - tests should skip gracefully if unavailable.

subtasks.title: Add workout audio integration tests
subtasks.description: Create tests that verify workout events trigger appropriate voice announcements. Use mock audio engine to verify the correct messages are generated.
subtasks.notes: Can mock the audio engine to capture speech text without actual audio output.

subtasks.title: Document platform-specific TTS notes
subtasks.description: Update documentation with any platform-specific requirements or notes (e.g., speech-dispatcher on Linux, required system components, known limitations).
subtasks.notes: Linux may require speech-dispatcher to be installed.

acceptance_criteria: TTS announces interval changes during workouts
User can select from available system voices
Speech rate and volume are configurable
TTS works on Windows, macOS, and Linux
